assembly.title: Aristotle — Athenian Constitution, part 41
assembly.context: §41 explains democratic votes in the Assembly and courts; Agyrrhius first introduces payment of one obol to encourage attendance. §43 describes turns for each of the ten tribes on the Council.

fourHundred.title: Thucydides — History of the Peloponnesian War, Book VIII §69
fourHundred.context: English Smith translation at §69.1 and §69.4: leaders of the oligarchy brought in the Four Hundred, who displaced the existing councillors.

fourHundredDate.title: Cambridge — Isonomia: The Dawn of Legal Equality
fourHundredDate.context: Section V timeline gives the oligarchic rule of the Four Hundred in 411–410 BCE and restoration in 410.

property.title: Aristotle — Rhetoric, Book I, forms of government
property.context: Defines oligarchic access to office as depending on property valuation.

polycrates.title: Thucydides — History of the Peloponnesian War, Book III §104.2
polycrates.context: Names Polycrates as tyrant of Samos and says he dedicated the conquered island Rhenea to Delian Apollo.

monarchy.title: Diogenes Laertius — Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Book III §83
monarchy.context: Distinguishes hereditary monarchy in Macedonia, where the king was selected from a certain family.

ostracism.title: Plutarch — Life of Aristides, chapter 7
ostracism.context: §7.4–5: archons first counted all ostraka; Plutarch says fewer than six thousand voters voided the procedure.

sherd.title: Athenian Agora Excavations — Ostrakon P 19615
sherd.context: Museum record identifies the inscribed ostrakon of Themistocles son of Neocles.

jury.title: ASCSA — The Athenian Agora XXVIII: The Lawcourts at Athens
jury.context: Published reconstruction (web lines 3451–3466) describes juror name plates in kleroterion slots and black and white dice matched to rows of five.

judicialText.title: Aristotle — Athenian Constitution, parts 51, 63–64
judicialText.context: §51: allotment of weights-and-measures officials. §63: name, father's name and deme on tickets. §64: black or white dice for choosing jurors.

scrutiny.title: Oxford Classical Dictionary — dokimasia
scrutiny.context: P. J. Rhodes identifies ancestral tombs, treatment of parents and witnesses at the archons' scrutiny; also distinguishes scrutiny of cavalry horses.

impeachment.title: Hyperides — In Defence of Euxenippus, §§7–8 and 39
impeachment.context: Burtt translation identifies the grounds under the impeachment law, including the bribed orator, and describes the charge against Euxenippus.

impeachmentTerm.title: Simon Fraser University — Cambridge Rhetorical Lexicon
impeachmentTerm.context: Entry Eisangelia explicitly names the procedure and the offense of giving harmful political advice for a bribe.

gaius.title: Gaius — Institutes, book I
gaius.context: §§48–50 independent and dependent persons; §§97–99 adoption and adrogation; §§113–117 manus and mancipium; §§132–134 triple mancipation, final release and alternative adoption.
